stories.headline: Xenophobia’s high price — why ConCourt’s defence of refugees matters for us all
stories.summary: The Constitutional Court’s refugee judgment protects constitutional rights. Misreading it fuels xenophobia, threatens democracy and imperils the rule of law.

stories.headline: The mini budget keeps SA diplomacy afloat, but structural rot still festers
stories.summary: The Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement offers Dirco a temporary lifeline, but underlying governance failures, unstaffed embassies and decaying overseas properties show South Africa’s diplomatic corps remains deeply in crisis.

stories.headline: Nepal to get $20m from climate fund after deadly August flood
stories.summary: KATHMANDU, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Nepal will receive $20m in aid from the United Nations' climate loss and damage fund after the devastating flood along its border with China’s Tibet region in August, the government said late on Thursday.

stories.headline: Microsoft develops AI tool that can diagnose ‘sequentially’ like a doctor
stories.summary: Oct 22 (Reuters) - Microsoft researchers say an AI tool that diagnoses patients step by step, as doctors do, was more than twice as accurate as general physicians at solving complex medical cases, according to a study published on Thursday in Science.

stories.headline: BOOK EXCERPT: Paradise found — A full-throttle view of Africa’s island treasures

stories.headline: POLAR POLITICS: China’s Antarctic marine protected area has a Soviet name, with more Russian fingerprints emerging
stories.summary: After a decade of blocking marine reserves with Moscow, Beijing seems to have unveiled its own - in a Soviet-named sea. stories.headline: CLEANING HOUSE: World body orders Athletics SA overhaul after president ousted for financial misconduct
stories.summary: Athletics South Africa has adopted the recommendation to remove rogue president James Moloi for misusing the federation’s credit. But World Athletics also wants the the athletics body to overhaul its leadership structure and constitution.

stories.headline: Hacking attempts surge as companies, governments rush to patch PHP flaws
stories.summary: TOKYO/BEIJING/AMSTERDAM, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Global firms and governments rushed on Thursday to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, as cloud firms reported a surge of hacking attempts after the vulnerabilities were disclosed.

stories.headline: Tunisian police clash with protesters in capital on day of heightened tensions
stories.summary: TUNIS, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Tunisian police fired tear gas to disperse protesters in Ettadhamen, a suburb of the capital, after the death of a man detained on suspicion of drug dealing, amid clashes with police in two towns in southern Tunisia.

stories.headline: Brazil may turn right-wing again — this is why South Africans should care
stories.summary: Brazil's upcoming presidential runoff election carries high stakes for South Africa, threatening key Global South partnerships, multilateral cooperation and shared commitments to human rights and democracy.

stories.headline: SA’s R13bn social grant cuts are arbitrary, cruel and economically short-sighted
stories.summary: The Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement cuts R13-billion from social grants, including child support and SRD grants. stories.headline: TITLE BECKONS: Maiden Formula One title in sight for phenom Kimi Antonelli
stories.summary: Formula 1 could crown its youngest champion at the Austin Grand Prix this Sunday, as teams start looking ahead to 2027.

stories.headline: BOOK EXTRACT: Rethinking Activism in Africa — activists as antibodies against a rotten social order
stories.summary: Rethinking Activism in Africa: Voices and Visionaries for Social Justice and Human Rights is a new book, edited by well-known activist and writer Mark Heywood. stories.headline: INSTANT CLASSIC: Veteran author delivers a baking bible for our time
stories.summary: The cookbook author who once introduced the red velvet cake to South Africa has brought out a 10th collection of baking recipes. It is so comprehensive – with more than 350 recipes – and thorough in its fine detail that it should be an instant classic.

stories.headline: All 14 Indians in yacht incident off Yemen coast reported safe, embassy says
stories.summary: All 14 Indian nationals on a yacht involved in an incident off Yemen's coast are reported safe, the Indian embassy in Yemen said on Friday.

stories.headline: Austria expels four Vienna-based Russian diplomats on security grounds
stories.summary: Austria's foreign ministry said on Friday it was expelling four Vienna-based Russian diplomats over "activities incompatible with their diplomatic status", a term usually used for spying.

stories.headline: Taiwan shuts down ahead of Typhoon Champi, nearly 1,000 flights cancelled
stories.summary: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday with the approach of Typhoon Champi, which was already bringing strong winds and torrential rain, and, while weakening, could still make direct landfall on the island.

stories.headline: Claude Monet’s ‘Iris’ becomes most expensive artwork sold at auction in France, Sotheby’s says
stories.summary: Claude Monet's "Iris" was sold late on Thursday for €50 million ($56.05 million), becoming the most expensive work of art sold at auction in France, Sotheby's said.

stories.headline: CONSTITUTION @ 30: Art, justice and Ruth Bader Ginsburg — Celebrating 30 years of the Constitutional Court
stories.summary: The 30th anniversary of South Africa’s democratic Constitution and the establishment of the country’s Constitutional Court gives us the opportunity to recall the creation of the court’s art collection, a speech at the court by US Supreme Court Associate Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, and a strategic engagement with the court by the US embassy.

stories.headline: CAMPUS SAFETY: Universities have policies to protect GBV victims, experts say, but not the will
stories.summary: A decade after Rhodes University students named alleged rapists, and New York revisits its laws following the Cornell case, experts say South African universities must protect student victims while cases are pending. stories.headline: ECO DECEPTION: How to spot greenwashing and mislabelled seafood in SA
stories.summary: From fluffy language to fake eco-labels and mislabelled fish, World Wild Fund for Nature’s Southern African Sustainable Seafood Initiative (WWF-Sassi) explains how consumers can identify greenwashing and make more sustainable seafood choices.

stories.headline: CRÉATION AFRICA: GuguByGugu uses mohair to fuse luxury streetwear with a rich African heritage
stories.summary: ‘There’s no shortage of quick, fast, cheap clothes,’ says Gugu Peteni, founder of GuguByGugu, a sustainable luxury fashion brand. What interests her instead is producing clothing that lasts and is made with intention.

stories.summary: The First Thing newsletter's Ever-lasting Subscriber Photo Gallery.

stories.headline: FROZEN POSTS: Qualified doctors desperate for jobs as KZN’s public hospitals go understaffed
stories.summary: They are qualified, ready and willing to serve their communities. But scores of doctors in KwaZulu-Natal are becoming increasingly desperate because of a lack of posts in government hospitals and clinics.

stories.headline: BHEKISISA: SA’s regulators are struggling to keep up with black market weight-loss jabs
stories.summary: South African regulators have won an important court battle against a pharmacy making its own versions of popular weight-loss injections. But illegal and experimental drugs are still being sold openly, while new rules to crack down on the trade are months away.

stories.headline: Preparing for the storm — grassroots action drives Durban’s climate disaster response
stories.summary: By combining immediate humanitarian relief with long-term urban planning, the Durban Coalition and Gift of the Givers demonstrate how grassroots solidarity can protect vulnerable communities from extreme weather.

stories.headline: MARKET THEATRE: Queer Fest kicks off: ‘Shockwave’ celebrates transformation over despair
stories.summary: Artistic director Greg Homann says The Market Theatre is about ‘the diversity of the South African voice’. It honours that tradition with its inaugural Queer Fest.

stories.headline: SUMMER SCORCHER: Weather service sounds El Niño alarm for North-East, including Kruger Park
stories.summary: While still a subject of intense debate among scientists, the strength of El Niño phases has been intensifying alarmingly in recent decades, pointing to the unnatural role of human-stoked climate change from the burning of fossil fuels – and this one is off the charts.

stories.headline: OFFLINE: SA’s Presidency website taken down as cybersecurity flaw sparks warnings across the world
stories.summary: South Africa’s Presidency announced on Friday that its website was temporarily unavailable because of a ‘global cybersecurity event’. This ‘event’ has affected countless individuals, businesses and governments globally, and sparked a series of warnings.

stories.headline: Are the French police the most violent in the EU?

stories.headline: Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
stories.summary: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

stories.summary: Names are central to our identity, so what happens when that name is a source of ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

stories.summary: US President Trump has said he wouldn't comment on who called for capping Ukraine's Starshield access but added that Elon Musk had "put it back." His account was rejected by Ukraine, which says nothing has changed.

stories.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul is joining counterparts in Turkey for discussions on a range of interlinked geopolitical crises. Back in Germany, the Bavarian CSU party begins its two-day conference in Munich.

stories.headline: Greece joins countries putting age-limits on social media, banning access for kids under 15
stories.summary: Greece has passed legislation banning social media access for children under 15. New rules will come into effect on January 1, 2027, and are designed to protect children's mental health.

stories.headline: Sri Lanka: Death of iconic elephant raises habitat concerns
stories.summary: The death of what was thought to be Sri Lanka’s largest elephant has drawn attention to human-elephant conflict in rural communities. The island country sees a high number of deadly encounters.

stories.headline: France: 1 killed, 4 wounded after shooting near Paris

stories.summary: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

stories.headline: Uganda says it has no active Ebola cases, but infections in Kenya and Nigeria are prompting fresh scrutiny
stories.summary: Health officials are investigating whether Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria crossed paths at Uganda's main airport as conflicting accounts cloud the source of one infection.

stories.headline: Japan-Russia ties erode as journalist sits in Moscow jail
stories.summary: Japan is demanding access to a journalist who was arrested by Russian security services. The Kremlin claims that Japan is using journalists as spies.

stories.headline: Many feared trapped under collapsed building in Nairobi
stories.summary: People are feared to be trapped after a large, unfinished building in Nairobi collapsed during construction. Rescue operations have proven complicated as police fired tear gas to disperse looters.

stories.summary: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

stories.headline: Afghan women could lose one of their last paths to a higher education

stories.headline: Russia, Ukraine agree to US-brokered, 1 city ceasefire
stories.summary: The Ukrainian city of Oleshky, occupied by Russia and on the frontline, faces a humanitarian crisis. The localized truce comes as Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said negotiators would meet for wider talks next month.

stories.summary: Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found.

stories.summary: NPR'S Leila Fadel speaks with retired four-star Gen. Joseph Votel about the war in Iran and the U.S. and Israeli objectives for a potential post-election bombing campaign.
